turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here and not at my desk with Owen's gradebook open? I want the zero off his essay.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so he could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. What does that history show that rules that out?
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
Okay. I'll ask Owen for the file. Whatever happens from here stays off his record, and it stays quiet. Is anything on his file right now?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
I will search it tonight. Students misquote from memory all the time, so what makes this more than a misquote? And what else do you have?

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.
I never mentioned December 1, but it's the right date. Fine, he'll do the rewrite Thursday to put this behind him. I want Thursday, Monday, private, and nothing on his record in that email tonight.
He'll be there Thursday. Send the email tonight.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Dear Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite in your room this Thursday, that you will mark it by Monday so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and that nothing goes on his record. I still expect those dates confirmed in writing, and an answer on whether anything is on his file right now. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday, marked by Monday, replacing the zero before December 1, and she still wants the dates and the clean record in writing plus an answer on whether anything is on his file now; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time never ran out.
What moved her: You answered her defence about drafting somewhere else by pointing to dates she could check herself, which gave her something to verify instead of an opinion.
What cost ground: You told her she had mentioned December 1 when she had not, a small slip she corrected flatly, and it cost you little.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history with its edit times just before midnight on the night before the essay was due came very close to that night, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what made the misquoted line more than a misquote, you moved straight to the rewrite, so answer that question first with something she could check on her own.
